translations.idiomatic: A sweeping reshuffle sent Wei Anshi to the eastern capital, rotated ministers, and cleared the inner council.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊寅，改太史監為太史局，依舊隸秘書省。

translations.literal: On wuyin of the eleventh month, the Astrological Directorate was changed to the Astrological Bureau, again subordinate to the Secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Astrological Directorate again became a Secretariat bureau.

sentences.zh: 改王師為傅。

translations.literal: The office of Royal Tutor was changed to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The Royal Tutor post was renamed Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 先天元年三年春正月辛未朔，親謁太廟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiantian, in spring, the first month, on xinwei the new moon, he personally visited the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiantian 1, on the xinwei new moon, he worshipped at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，上始釋慘服，御正殿受朝賀。

translations.literal: On guiyou, he first laid aside deep mourning garb, attended the main hall, and received court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou he ended deep mourning, took the main throne, and accepted New Year homage.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，並、汾、絳三州地震，壞人廬舍。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Bing, Fen, and Jiang prefectures suffered earthquake; people’s dwellings were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu earthquakes wrecked homes in Bing, Fen, and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，南郊。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the southern suburb rite.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi he sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 戊子，躬耕籍田。

translations.literal: On wuzi, he personally plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi he plowed the sacred field himself.

sentences.zh: 己丑，大赦天下，改元為太極。

translations.literal: On jichou, a great amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven; the era name was changed to Taiji.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the realm was amnestied and the reign title became Taiji.

sentences.zh: 內外官四品已下加一階，三品已上加爵一級。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials of fourth rank and below received one rank; third rank and above each received one noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Officers to fourth rank rose one step; third rank and up gained a noble grade.

sentences.zh: 孔宣父祠廟，本州取側近三十戶以供灑掃。

translations.literal: For the temple of the Venerable Master Kong, thirty nearby households in that prefecture were taken to sweep and sprinkle.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius’ temple was given thirty local households for upkeep.

sentences.zh: 天下大酺五日，特賜老人九十已上緋衫牙笏，八十已上綠衫木笏。

translations.literal: The realm enjoyed great feasting for five days; the aged ninety and above were specially granted scarlet robes and ivory court tablets, eighty and above green robes and wooden tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Five days of feasting were proclaimed; men over ninety got scarlet and ivory tablets, over eighty green and wood.

sentences.zh: 乙未，戶部尚書岑羲、左臺御史大夫竇懷貞並同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Minister of Revenue Cen Xi and Left Censor-in-Chief Dou Huai’zhen were both made Grand Counselors of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Cen Xi and Dou Huai’zhen joined the third-rank council.

sentences.zh: 二月丁酉，秘書增少監一員，光祿、大理、鴻臚、太府、衛尉、宗正各增置少卿一員，少府監、將作監增置少監一員，國子監增置司業一員，左右臺各增置中丞一員。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the Secretariat gained one additional Vice Director; the Directorates of Palace Receptions, Justice, State Guests, the Grand Treasury, Court of the Imperial Clan, and Imperial Sacrifices each gained a Vice Director; the Directorates of the Palace Workshops and Imperial Construction each gained a Vice Director; the Directorate of Education gained a Vice Chancellor; the Left and Right Censorates each gained an Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou a wave of vice posts was added across the secretariat, ministries, censorate, and schools.

sentences.zh: 雍洛二州、並益荊揚四大都督府各增置司馬一員，仍分為左右司馬。

translations.literal: The two capitals of Yong and Luo and the four great area commands of Bing, Yi, Jing, and Yang each gained a Chief Administrator, divided into Left and Right Chief Administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, Luo, and the four great commands of Bing, Yi, Jing, and Yang each gained left and right chief administrators.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，皇太子釋奠於國學。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the crown prince performed the libation rite at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the heir offered at the National University.

sentences.zh: 追贈顏回為太子太師，曾參為太子太保。

translations.literal: Yan Hui was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; Zeng Shen Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Hui and Zeng Shen were posthumously honored as the heir’s grand tutor and protector.

sentences.zh: 每年春秋釋奠，以四科弟子、曾參從祀，列於二十二賢之上。

translations.literal: Each spring and autumn libation, the four categories of disciples and Zeng Shen were associated in sacrifice, ranked above the twenty-two worthies.
translations.idiomatic: At spring and autumn rites Zeng Shen and the four disciple categories stood above the twenty-two sages.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，廢右御史臺官員。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the offices of the Right Censorate were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the Right Censorate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 己巳，頒新格式於天下。

translations.literal: On jisi, the new statutes and formats were promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi new law codes went out to the empire.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛丑，制曰：

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinchou, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on xinchou, an edict ran:

sentences.zh: 五月戊寅，親祀北郊。

translations.literal: On wuyin of the fifth month, he personally sacrificed at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin of the fifth month he worshipped at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 辛未，大赦天下，改元為延和。

translations.literal: On xinwei, a great amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven; the era name was changed to Yanhe.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the realm was amnestied and the reign title became Yanhe.

sentences.zh: 桓彥範、敬暉、崔玄暐、張柬之、袁恕己等，特還其子孫實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuoji, and others specially had their sons and grandsons restored to a substantive fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The sons and grandsons of Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jianzhi, Yuan Shuoji, and their fellows regained two-hundred-household fiefs.

sentences.zh: 天下大酺五日。

translations.literal: The realm enjoyed great feasting for five days.
translations.idiomatic: Five days of public feasting were proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 六月癸丑，戶部尚書岑羲為侍中。

translations.literal: On guichou of the sixth month, Minister of Revenue Cen Xi was made Attendant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Cen Xi became Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，追奠則天皇后曰天后聖帝。

translations.literal: On yimao, the late Empress Zetian was posthumously honored as Empress of the Sage Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Wu Zetian was posthumously styled Empress of the Sage Emperor.

sentences.zh: 庚申，幽州都督孫儉率左驍衛將軍李楷洛、左威衛將軍周以悌等，將兵三萬，與奚首領李大輔戰於硎山，為賊所敗，儉沒於陣。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Youzhou Area Commander Sun Jian led Left Valiant Cavalry General Li Kailuo, Left Martial Guard General Zhou Yiti, and others with thirty thousand troops to battle the Xi chieftain Li Dafu at Mount Xing; they were defeated by the bandits and Jian died in the array.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Sun Jian of Youzhou fell at Mount Xing fighting Li Dafu of the Xi with thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，魏知古為戶部尚書，仍依舊同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On renxu, Wei Zhigu was made Minister of Revenue, still Grand Counselor of the third rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Wei Zhigu took Revenue while keeping his council seat.

sentences.zh: 秋七月庚午，竇懷貞為尚書右僕射，平章軍國重事。

translations.literal: On gengwu of the seventh month, Dou Huai’zhen was made Right Vice Director and “equal” in managing weighty affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Dou Huai’zhen became Right Vice Director with charge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 己卯，上觀樂於安福門，以燭繼晝，經日乃止。

translations.literal: On jimao, the emperor watched music at Anfu Gate; candles carried day into night and only ended after a full day.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao he watched music at Anfu Gate by candlelight from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 八月庚子，帝傳位於皇太子，自稱太上皇帝，五日一度受朝於太極殿，自稱曰朕，三品已上除授及大刑獄，並自決之，其處分事稱誥、令。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the emperor transmitted the throne to the crown prince, styled himself Retired Emperor, and every five days received court once at Taiji Hall; he called himself zhen; appointments and great punishments for third rank and above he decided himself, his orders styled gao and ling.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he abdicated to the heir, took the title Retired Emperor, and every five days held court at Taiji as zhen, reserving third-rank appointments and capital crimes under gao and ling.

sentences.zh: 皇帝每日受朝於武德殿，自稱曰予，三品已下除授及徒罪並令決之，其處分事稱制、敕。

translations.literal: The emperor daily received court at Wude Hall, styled himself yu; appointments and penal exile for third rank and below he ordered decided, his orders styled zhi and chi.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor held daily court at Wude as yu, deciding lower ranks and lesser punishments by zhi and chi.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，大赦天下，改元為先天。

translations.literal: On jiachen, a great amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven; the era name was changed to Xiantian.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the realm was amnestied and the reign title became Xiantian.

sentences.zh: 八月戊申，皇帝子許昌王嗣直改封郯王，真定王嗣謙為郢王。

translations.literal: On wushen of the eighth month, the emperor’s son Prince of Xuchang Sizhi was re-enfeoffed Prince of Tan and Prince of Zhending Siqian Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Sizhi became Prince of Tan and Siqian Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以宋王成器為司空，依舊遙領揚州大都督。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Prince of Song Chengqi was made Minister of Works, still holding Yangzhou Grand Commandery from afar as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Chengqi became Minister of Works while still titular Yangzhou commander.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，竇懷貞為尚書左僕射、同中書門下三品，仍兼御史大夫；

translations.literal: On gengxu, Dou Huai’zhen was made Left Vice Director and Grand Counselor of the third rank, still also Censor-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Dou Huai’zhen became Left Vice Director and chief censor;

sentences.zh: 劉幽求為尚書右僕射，依舊同中書門下三品；

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu was made Right Vice Director, still Grand Counselor of the third rank as before;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu became Right Vice Director with council rank;

sentences.zh: 魏知古為侍中；

translations.literal: Wei Zhigu was made Attendant-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhigu became Attendant-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 崔湜為中書令；

translations.literal: Cui Shi was made Grand Counselor;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shi became Grand Counselor;

sentences.zh: 並監修國史。

translations.literal: all supervised revision of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: all four oversaw the national history.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，立皇帝妃王氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the emperor’s consort Lady Wang was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Lady Wang became empress.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，劉幽求配流封州。

translations.literal: On guihai, Liu Youqiu was sentenced to penal exile in Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Liu Youqiu was exiled to Feng.

sentences.zh: 九月丁卯朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On dingmao the new moon of the ninth month, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth month’s dingmao new moon brought a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 甲申，封皇帝子嗣升為陜王。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the emperor’s son Sisheng was enfeoffed Prince of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Sisheng became Prince of Shan.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚子，皇帝親謁太廟，禮畢，御延喜門，大赦天下。

translations.literal: On gengzi of the tenth month of winter, the emperor personally visited the Grand Temple; when the rites were complete, he attended from Yanxi Gate and proclaimed a great amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi he worshipped at the Grand Temple, then from Yanxi Gate amnestied the realm.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，祔昭成皇后、肅明皇后神主於儀坤廟。

translations.literal: On renyin, the spirit tablets of Empresses Zhaocheng and Suming were enshrined in Yikun Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the tablets of Empresses Zhaocheng and Suming entered Yikun Temple.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，皇帝幸新豐之溫湯，校獵於渭川。

translations.literal: On guimao, the emperor visited the hot springs at Xinfeng and hunted on the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao he bathed at Xinfeng and hunted the Wei.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁未，誥禁人屠殺犬雞。

translations.literal: On dingwei of the twelfth month, a gao forbade people to slaughter dogs and chickens.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month a gao banned slaughter of dogs and chickens.

sentences.zh: 戊午，改箕州為儀州。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Ji Prefecture was changed to Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Ji became Yi.

sentences.zh: 先天二年二年春正月，敕河北諸州團結兵馬，皆令本州刺史押掌。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiantian, in spring, the first month, an edict ordered the military forces of Hebei circuits to be mustered, all to be led by their prefectural governors.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiantian 2 an edict put Hebei militia under their prefects’ command.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，吏部尚書兼太子右諭德、酂國公蕭至忠為中書令。

translations.literal: On yihai, Minister of Personnel and Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Xiao Zhizhong, Duke of Zan, was made Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Xiao Zhizhong, Duke of Zan, became Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 上元日夜，上皇御安福門觀燈，出內人連袂踏歌，縱百僚觀之，一夜方罷。

translations.literal: On the Lantern Festival night the Retired Emperor attended lamps at Anfu Gate; palace women linked arms in street songs; all officials were allowed to watch; only at night’s end did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: On Lantern Night the retired emperor watched lamps at Anfu Gate while palace women danced in the streets before the court until dawn.

sentences.zh: 二月丙申，改隆州為閬州，始州為劍州。

translations.literal: On bingshen of the second month, Longzhou was changed to Langzhou and Shi Prefecture to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Long became Lang and Shi became Jian.

sentences.zh: 分冀州置深州。

translations.literal: Shen Prefecture was established by dividing Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was split to create Shen.

sentences.zh: 初，有僧婆陀請夜開門然燈百千炬，三日三夜。

translations.literal: Earlier, a monk Boduo requested that the gates be opened at night with a thousand torches lit for three days and three nights.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the monk Boduo had asked for three nights of open gates and a thousand lamps.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御延喜門觀燈縱樂，凡三日夜。

translations.literal: The emperor attended lamps at Yanxi Gate and indulged in music for three days and three nights.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor watched lamps at Yanxi Gate and feasted three full nights.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺嚴挺之上疏諫之，乃止。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Yan Tingzhi submitted a memorial remonstrating; only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Yan Tingzhi remonstrated and the revels ended.

sentences.zh: 三月辛卯，皇后祀先蠶。

translations.literal: On xinmao of the third month, the empress sacrificed to the Silkworm Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the empress offered to the Silkworm Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，制敕表狀、書奏、箋牒年月等數，作一十、三十、四十字。

translations.literal: On guisi, the number of characters in edicts, tables, memorials, petitions, and notes for year and month was set at ten, thirty, and forty characters.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi document headings were standardized to ten-, thirty-, and forty-character lines.

sentences.zh: 夏六月丙辰，兵部尚書、朔方道行軍大總管郭元振加同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, on bingchen, Minister of War and Commander-in-Chief of the Shuofang campaign Guo Yuanzhen was given added rank as Grand Counselor of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Guo Yuanzhen of Shuofang gained a third-rank council seat.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲子，太平公主與僕射竇懷貞、侍中岑羲、中書令蕭至忠、左羽林大將軍常元楷等謀逆，事覺，皇帝率兵誅之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on jiazi, Princess Taiping with Vice Director Dou Huai’zhen, Attendant-in-Chief Cen Xi, Grand Counselor Xiao Zhizhong, General of the Left Feathered Forest Chang Yuankai, and others plotted rebellion; the plot was discovered and the emperor led troops to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Taiping, Dou Huai’zhen, Cen Xi, Xiao Zhizhong, Chang Yuankai, and others plotted treason; the emperor crushed them by force.

sentences.zh: 窮其黨與，太子少保薛稷、左散騎常侍賈膺福、右羽林將軍李慈李欽、中書舍人李猷、中書令崔湜、尚書左丞盧藏用、太史令傅孝忠、僧惠範等皆誅之。

translations.literal: Investigating their party, Junior Protector of the Heir Apparent Xue Ji, Left Regular Attendant Jia Yingfu, Right Feathered Forest General Li Ci and Li Qin, Palace Draftsman Li You, Grand Counselor Cui Shi, Left Assistant Director Lu Zangyong, Astrological Director Fu Xiaozhong, the monk Huifan, and others were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The purge took Xue Ji, Jia Yingfu, the Li brothers, Cui Shi, Lu Zangyong, Fu Xiaozhong, Huifan, and the rest to execution.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書郭元振從上御承天門樓，大赦天下，自大闢罪已下，無輕重咸赦除之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Guo Yuanzhen followed the emperor to Chengtian Gate tower; a great amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven; from great sedition downward, none light or heavy was not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuanzhen stood with the emperor on Chengtian Gate and amnestied all crimes down from great sedition.

sentences.zh: 翌日，太上皇誥曰：』朕將高居無為，自今後軍國刑政一事以上，並取皇帝處分。

translations.literal: The next day the Retired Emperor’s gao said: “I shall dwell aloft in nonaction; from now on for military, penal, and political affairs of any kind and above, all shall follow the emperor’s disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the retired emperor’s gao read: “I take the high seat of nonaction; henceforth all military and civil matters go to the emperor.

translations.literal: ” — closing quotation of the gao.
translations.idiomatic: [Close of gao.]

sentences.zh: 開元四年夏六月甲子，太上皇帝崩於百福殿，時年五十五。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer, jiazi, of the fourth year of Kaiyuan, the Retired Emperor died in Baifu Hall at age fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 4, sixth month, the retired emperor died in Baifu Hall at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己亥，上尊謚曰大聖貞皇帝，廟曰睿宗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on jihai, the posthumous title Great Sage and Chaste Emperor was elevated; his temple name was Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was posthumously named Great Sage and Chaste Emperor, temple name Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚午，葬於橋陵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on gengwu, he was buried at Qiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was buried at Qiaoling.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載二月，改謚曰玄真大聖大興孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year of Tianbao, the posthumous title was changed to Emperor Xuanzhen the Great Sage, Great Prosperity, and Great Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 13 his posthumous style was lengthened to Xuanzhen the Great Sage of Great Prosperity and Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 【史評】史臣曰：法不一則奸偽起，政不一則朋黨生，上既啟其泉源，下胡息於奔競。

translations.literal: 【Historian’s appraisal】 The historian says: When law is not one, fraud and falsehood arise; when government is not one, factions are born; when the ruler opens the springhead, how can those below cease scrambling in competition?
translations.idiomatic: 【Historian’s appraisal】 The historian writes: One law or the realm fills with fraud; one government or cliques multiply; when the throne opens the floodgate, who below can stop striving?

sentences.zh: 觀夫天后之時，雲委於二張之第；

translations.literal: Consider the time of the Empress: clouds piled at the mansions of the Two Zhangs;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Empress, favor pooled in the Two Zhangs’ halls;

sentences.zh: 孝和之世，波注于三王之門。

translations.literal: in the age of Xiaohé, waves poured at the gates of the Three Princes.
translations.idiomatic: under Xiaohé, tide ran to the Three Princes’ doors.

sentences.zh: 獻奇則除設盈庭，納賄則斜封滿路，咸以進趨相軌，奸利是圖，如火投泉，安得無敗？

translations.literal: Offer marvels and posts filled the court; pay bribes and slant-seal appointments choked the roads—all advancing by the track of promotion, plotting profit as their chart, like fire cast into a spring: how could there be no ruin?
translations.idiomatic: Wonder-workers packed the hall; bribes bought “slant-seal” posts on every road—everyone raced for gain like fire poured into a spring: could ruin not follow?

sentences.zh: 洎景龍繼統，污俗廓清，然猶投杼於乘輿之間，抵掌於太平之日。

translations.literal: When Jinglong succeeded, foul custom was swept clear, yet still the mother tested the carriage with a pestle and clapped hands on Taiping’s day.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglong brought a cleaner court, yet a mother still tested the throne and a sister still ruled the feast.

sentences.zh: 以至書頻告變，上不自安，宮臣致禦魅之科，天子慊巡邊之詔。

translations.literal: So that letters repeatedly reported omens, the ruler could not rest secure; palace officers proposed charms against evil spirits, the Son of Heaven issued an edict ashamed to tour the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Omens piled in the mail; the ruler slept uneasy; palace magicians offered anti-demon rites; he shamefacedly ordered border tours.

sentences.zh: 彼既彎弓而射我，我則號泣以行刑。

translations.literal: They had already bent the bow to shoot at me; I could only weep as I carried out the execution.
translations.idiomatic: They drew the bow on me; I wept even as I struck.

sentences.zh: 此雖鎮國之尤，亦是臨軒之失。

translations.literal: This was chiefly the fault of the Princess of Zhenguo, yet also a failure at the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping bore the greater blame, yet the throne too had failed.

sentences.zh: 夫君人孝愛，錫之以典刑，納之於軌物，俾無僭逼，下絕覬覦，自然治道惟新，亂階不作。

translations.literal: Now the ruler’s filial love should bestow canonical punishment and draw kin within the measure of ritual, so that none overstep and those below cease coveting—then naturally the Way of rule would be renewed and the steps to chaos unmade.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler’s love should punish by statute and bind kin to ritual, leaving no overreach and no hungry eyes below—then order would renew itself and chaos never rise.

sentences.zh: 孝和既已失之，玄真亦未為得。

translations.literal: Xiaohé had already failed in this; Xuanzhen likewise did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaohé missed it; Xuanzhen did not do better.

sentences.zh: 【贊】贊曰：孝和、玄真，皆肖先人。

translations.literal: 【Eulogy】 The eulogy says: Xiaohé and Xuanzhen both resembled their forebears.
translations.idiomatic: 【Eulogy】 The eulogy says: Xiaohé and Xuanzhen both took after their ancestors.

sentences.zh: 率情背禮，取樂於身。

translations.literal: Following feeling and turning their backs on ritual, they took pleasure for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They followed appetite, broke ritual, and kept joy for themselves.

sentences.zh: 夷塗不履，覆轍攸遵。

translations.literal: They would not walk the level road but followed the overturned cart’s track.
translations.idiomatic: They shunned the level path and rode the rut of the overturned cart.

sentences.zh: 扶持聖嗣，賴有賢臣。

translations.literal: To uphold the sacred heir they relied on worthy ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Only worthy ministers bore up the sacred heir.
